fleetscan.name: FleetScan
fleetscan.tagline: Fleet incidents, field scan, manager oversight
fleetscan.role: Product design, frontend architecture, Supabase integration, authentication, and scan workflow ownership.

meta.title: FleetScan - Case study
meta.description: Fleet incident operations app with QR flow, role model, RLS, and strict validation.

paragraphs: Field teams need to report a truck status in seconds, without friction and without unstable manual entry.
Managers need a reliable fleet view without heavy enterprise tooling or fragile shared spreadsheets.
Mobile-first workflow: scan by QR or plate, open the vehicle sheet, and make a binary report (damage vs nothing to report).
Lean Supabase backend: SSR auth, role-scoped RLS, versioned SQL migrations, and strict server-side validation.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: FleetScan (scratch_tracker repository) addresses a real depot workflow where speed and clarity matter more than feature volume.
The MVP covers the driver journey plus a staff overview, while the roadmap openly tracks photos, Realtime, and stronger cache strategy.
bullets: Concrete field constraints shape every UX decision
Scope is deliberate to avoid fake completeness
Roadmap remains technical and product-aligned

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Routing is organized with `(splash)`, `(public)`, and `(protected)` groups to keep responsibilities explicit.
A feature / controller / view structure drives scan flows, truck dashboard behavior, and fleet overview composition.
bullets: lib/ includes Zod schemas, server actions, and plate/date mappers
Supabase SSR session middleware handles authenticated boundaries
Around 30 Vitest tests cover critical business logic

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: fr / nl / en localization is cookie-based to keep URLs stable for multi-country field usage.
Zod at the boundaries enforces a strict rule: external data is never trusted by default.
bullets: No over-abstraction: one function per file and isolated features
Camera scanning is isolated in its own dedicated module
Shared RLS rules are versioned and documented in SQL migrations

execution.title: Execution and next steps
paragraphs: The foundation is production-oriented: tests are in place, product documentation exists, and the structure scales without rewrite pressure.
Next steps are explicit: field captures, final create flow completion, and Vercel deployment with monitoring.
bullets: Core architecture is mature enough for hardening
Last-mile delivery is identified, not hidden
Monitoring is planned as part of shipping, not afterthought

shadow.name: Shadow
shadow.tagline: Private communication and planning for a closed circle
shadow.role: Fullstack implementation on Next.js and Supabase: messaging, calendar workflows, PWA setup, and security hardening.

meta.title: Shadow - Case study
meta.description: Private messaging and shared calendar app with Realtime, PWA delivery, RLS, and E2E tests.

paragraphs: A restricted group needs a private communication space with disappearing messages and shared planning, without depending on public consumer tools.
The experience must remain smooth on mobile, install like a native app, and keep technical behavior predictable.
The stack combines Next.js and Supabase with SSR auth, modular CRUD per domain entity, and Realtime updates for threads and badges.
PWA support is production-configured through manifest, service worker, and explicit middleware exclusions to avoid deployment surprises.

context.title: Context
paragraphs: Shadow combines 24-hour ephemeral messaging, direct and group conversations, and an events calendar in one coherent private product.
Fourteen SQL migrations version the data model, and architecture/security documents include pre-deployment audit findings.
bullets: Product scope is coherent, not feature-stacked
Data model evolution is tracked through migrations
Audit output directly informs implementation priorities

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The codebase is split by feature domains (auth, messages, calendar, home) to preserve ownership clarity.
Entity-level `lib/supabase/CRUD/` modules maintain readability and make integration testing straightforward.
bullets: SWR provides responsive caching behavior for message flows
Supabase Storage handles media payloads
Middleware combines getClaims() checks and auth rate limiting

decisions.title: Decisions
paragraphs: RLS is treated as the primary security boundary, with known pitfalls documented transparently, including conversation access edge cases.
Framer Motion interactions are wrapped with reduced-motion handling for sensitive or high-frequency UX moments.
bullets: Explicit webpack settings ensure PWA and Vercel compatibility
Bundle analysis is integrated to keep performance under control
Five Playwright specs currently secure the auth-critical surface

execution.title: Execution
paragraphs: The MVP is advanced and credible, with final hardening still required (notably CSP and error boundary reinforcement).
It demonstrates a complete technical product lifecycle, not only visual frontend output.
bullets: Core product behavior is stable in real conditions
Remaining security items are known and actionable
Delivery narrative stays honest about what is left

spill-crumb.name: Spill Crumb
spill-crumb.tagline: Anonymous confessions with realtime feed and platform governance
spill-crumb.role: Fullstack platform architecture and development: auth, paginated feed, synchronized stores, realtime notifications, anti-spam, admin sponsoring/logs, and full CI/E2E pipeline.

meta.title: Spill Crumb - Case study
meta.description: Anonymous social network: feed, reactions, realtime notifications, anti-spam, and admin back-office in production.

paragraphs: The product targets a space where users share stories and confessions under a pseudonym, freedom of expression without exposing real identity.
An anonymous social feed must handle volume, spam, and abuse without weighing down the experience. The 5 posts/day limit and rate limiting are explicit product guardrails.
Admin needs visibility: sponsoring, platform logs, and stats, without opening the codebase to understand system health.
I modeled decoupled post stores (feed, profile, live detail) with centralized fan-out via lib/post-store-sync, one mutation propagates cleanly everywhere.
Supabase realtime is reserved for high-immediate-value interactions (feed, notifications, navbar badge), not applied everywhere by default.
Assumed trade-off: soft launch without mandatory Upstash (in-memory fallback per instance), documented and recommended before marketing scale campaigns.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Spill The Crumbs is available in fr / en / es, responsive across mobile-tablet-desktop, deployed on Vercel from main.
16 product modules cover auth, onboarding, home, posts, profile, notifications, settings, add-new-post, and admin.
MVP is production-ready: email/password auth, stable backend, operational admin tools, with assumed limitations (post reporting, password reset) on the roadmap.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: ProtectedFeaturePage pattern: centralized auth, typed loaders, i18n errors via AppFeatureError. Each feature follows screen + sections + services/hooks.
Mutations via next-safe-action + Zod. Separate Supabase clients browser / server / admin (service_role never exposed client-side).
bullets: post-feed-store, profile-posts-store, live-store + sync handler registry
post_stats triggers, top drama RPC, Postgres RLS
Upstash rate limit (auth, reactions, comments) + in-memory fallback
638+ Vitest tests, CI deps audit + coverage + local Supabase E2E

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: The 5 posts/day limit is enforced app-side AND via DB trigger, defense in depth against client bypass.
The /admin/logs dashboard persists platform events with widgets and pagination, lightweight alternative to observability SaaS for MVP.
bullets: Mutation fan-out rather than coupled monolithic stores
Cookie-based i18n without URL segment · 3 locales, en fallback
Husky pre-commit + develop → main pipeline with Vercel previews
Post reporting and verification emails deferred · transparent roadmap

execution.title: Execution and next steps
paragraphs: Product is live in soft launch / internal testing with post-deploy checklist (auth, realtime feed, notifications).
Test coverage (638+ unit, 7 E2E specs) secures evolution on a rich domain (feed, reactions, comments, sponsoring).
Next increments: report moderation, Upstash before scale campaign, password reset and confirmation emails.

jikowood.name: Jikowood
jikowood.tagline: Turn a craftsperson site into a credible premium experience
jikowood.role: End-to-end frontend rebuild: experience direction (splash, hero, gallery), feature-first architecture, fr/en/nl i18n, GSAP motion with reduced-motion, and Vitest/Playwright quality gates.

meta.title: Jikowood · Frontend case study
meta.description: Premium showcase rebuild for a carpenter: immersive gallery, Belgian trilingual i18n, feature-first architecture, and E2E tests.

paragraphs: The client needed a web presence matching a high-end atelier, not a generic template. The site had to communicate precision, modernity, and craftsmanship immediately.
Photographed projects are the main argument. Without a fluid gallery journey, photos stay a grid; with immersive navigation, they become proof and desire.
The Belgian context requires trilingual support (fr / en / nl) from day one. Bolting i18n on later would have broken URLs and SEO coherence.
I set a feature-first architecture: App Router orchestrates, logic lives in features/ and lib/. Goal: ship fast without losing readability for a possible CMS later.
GSAP motion serves brand entry and the gallery, not scroll for scroll's sake. prefers-reduced-motion is respected from the animation hooks.
Assumed trade-off: 100% static content and UI-only contact (local success). The client can already judge craft; real email delivery and the jikowood.be cutover come next.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: JIKOWOOD is a woodworking atelier (Micro Factory, Molenbeek) targeting custom interiors. The showcase must convince before the first call.
Five indexed projects (Cannes, Knokke, Krainem, Overijs, Uccle) ground storytelling in real photography, not placeholders.
Delivery targets a Vercel validation URL; jikowood.be switches once contact and content are locked.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Dynamic [slug] and [slug]/[projectSlug] routes generate presentation, services, gallery, and contact pages per locale, without a /fr URL prefix.
Boundaries stay clean: app/ for routing, features/ for product UI, lib/ for i18n, motion, projects, and SEO. Conventions are documented in the client repo.
bullets: Typed fr / en / nl messages + language cookie
Static project index (~43 JPEGs under public/projects/)
Fullscreen gallery navigation as pure tested functions
SEO: sitemap, robots, security headers, next/font

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: I prioritized visible craft (splash, notch hero, gallery) and engineering discipline (tests, docs) over a premature backend on a still-validating showcase.
Contact stays intentionally UI-only: wiring Formspree too early would freeze a flow before the client validated the journey.
bullets: Do not claim Lenis / ScrollTrigger until they are wired
Custom i18n fitted to Belgian slugs rather than forcing next-intl
Playwright E2E on splash, services, contact, and fullscreen
Defer CMS / admin while content lives in the repo

execution.title: Execution and next steps
paragraphs: The rebuild is live at https://jikowood-refonte.vercel.app, full journeys navigable in three languages.
Next increments: wire real contact delivery, lock content, cut over the client domain, and optionally add a light CMS.
The north star remains premium frontend craft with a maintainable architecture, not an effects demo.

ttc-v0.name: Take The Crown (3x3)
ttc-v0.tagline: Model the sport before the code, then ship a trustworthy slice
ttc-v0.role: I set the 3x3 product vision (Identity, Competition, Reputation), the domain/architecture documentation, and the MVP implementation: Player/Organizer auth, Geoapify events, verified matches, and World/Country ranking on Next.js + Supabase.

meta.title: Take The Crown 3x3 · Case study
meta.description: 3x3 basketball platform: domain model, Event→Verified→Ranking slice, defense-in-depth AuthZ, and Next.js + Supabase MVP.

paragraphs: The 3x3 ecosystem is split across social networks, organizer sites, registrations, rankings, and chat apps. No single place owns both identity and history.
Without an Event → Match → Verified Result chain, rankings become noise: self-report, unauthorized scores, point farming.
The product must serve players, teams, organizers, and fans without replacing federations: a universal digital layer, not another isolated tournament tool.
Guiding principle: Identity Over Events. Model the sport (actors, competition, ranking) before stacking screens. Documented ≠ Implemented ≠ MVP stays explicit in the docs.
MVP targets the Identity → Event → Match → Result → Ranking → Discovery slice, not a truncated product with no end-to-end value.
Pragmatic stack: Next.js + Supabase monolith (Auth, Postgres+RLS, Storage). No public API or search microservices until data trust is proven.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Three pillars: Identity, Competition, Reputation. Ubiquitous language: User, Player, Team, Organization/Organizer, Match, Result, Ranking (≠ Rating ≠ Leaderboard).
Take The Crown 3x3 is distinct from the 1v1 league in the same brand universe: different codebase, different model (multi-events vs 1v1 league).
Docs also cover brackets, circuits, Opportunity, Multi-Tenancy… intentionally broader than shipped code, to guide increments without improvisation.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Feature-based frontend (auth, create, events, profile, ranking) plus an admin panel behind ADMIN_PANEL_PATH (server rewrite, slug out of the client bundle, profiles.role = admin).
Defense-in-depth AuthZ: Server Actions (requireEventAuthor) + Postgres RLS + author checks inside ranking RPCs, even via service_role.
Events: public creation with mandatory Geoapify address (address, place_id, lat/lng). Public profiles at opaque URLs /profile/[username]-[publicId], public_id ≠ auth.uid.
bullets: Platform MVP roles: player | organizer | admin
Profile UI fork: Player = media gallery; Organizer = Draft/Upcoming/Passed counts
Public Storage buckets (avatars, profile-media) assumed for MVP
Synchronous ranking award via RPC after verified matches

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Create = Event only: no Add Score entry in nav. Scores stay reserved to the event author; points only after verified status.
Next + Supabase monolith for MVP velocity: one stack and native RLS; public API and dedicated search engines deferred.
Private events, brackets, OAuth, ELO, livestream, and billing are out of MVP (Under construction UI or absent), even when present in the domain model.
bullets: Score self-report abandoned to protect rankings
In-memory rate-limit acceptable for MVP; Redis later if multi-instance
CSP enforce deferred (P2) after asset inventory
List search: soft place_id match or ~1.5 km proximity

execution.title: Execution and next steps
paragraphs: Shipped: email auth Player/Organizer, own-only settings, event CRUD (Geoapify, public), draft→verified matches, W/L points, /ranking World/Country, Player gallery, admin monitoring.
Partial: separate Player domain entity, competition/brackets, full ranking formula (Best 5, event weights, cursor pagination), Registration workflow on the product side.
Live at https://take-the-crown-v001.vercel.app/. Next value: lock useful Registration/brackets and harden ranking before expanding the documented domain further.

Scroll one-pager with localized section slugs.

architecture.title: Architecture

Locale middleware + cookie; sitemap aligned on translated sections.
bullets: Localized section routes
Zod form validation
GSAP splash + Framer modals
Vitest on locale resolution

Mock testimonials are explicit, better than fake social proof sold as real.
bullets: EmailJS for contact (not Formspree)
Default locale nl
One-pager over multi-page marketing

paragraphs: A strategic holding needs a sober credible presence, not a startup template.
Learn–Earn–Return and the consultant network must be understandable without a pitch deck.
Real contact had to be immediate; structured booking could wait until 2027.
Single scroll page with section menu and GSAP motion polish.
FR/EN i18n via next-intl.
Roundtable contact via Web3Forms; booking calendar UI gated as Coming Soon 2027.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Positioning: international strategic catalyst around Learn / Earn / Return.
Consultant network supports dialogue and matching, not an open marketplace.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Feature components (hero, philosophy, network, contact…) and shared section primitives.
SEO: OG, JSON-LD, robots, sitemap.
bullets: Members as TypeScript data (3 profiles)
Internal DRY/SOLID docs
No automated test suite

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Network content kept intentionally small to stay credible.
2027 booking is an explicit product gate, UI prepares without promising real confirmation today.
bullets: Web3Forms + env key
next-intl over custom i18n
Frontend polish focus

execution.title: Execution and next steps

nana.name: Hors Cadre

nana.role: I designed and shipped the full product: public gallery, Supabase atelier, perf/SEO/i18n, and tests through production.

meta.description: Photographer portfolio: ISR gallery, Supabase admin atelier, Liquid Glass, and E2E tests in production.

paragraphs: A premium photo portfolio must immerse without friction, no visitor accounts.
The photographer must publish and reorder large volumes without a heavy CMS.
Public SEO surface and private atelier must stay clearly separated.
Public ISR vs admin via env segments + Server Actions, no exposed REST API.
Client-side WebP before Storage; album images in JSONB (ADR).
Mono-admin: signup closed after the first account.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Hors Cadre brand: Liquid Glass aesthetic, free download of public photos.
fr / nl / en i18n via cookie, no URL prefix.

architecture.title: Architecture

Single Supabase backend; ADR-001→015 document irreversible choices.
bullets: 640px thumbs + 300s ISR cache
Obscured admin segments
~455 Vitest tests + public/atelier E2E
Upload up to 1,500 photos

Obscure admin URL + RLS: defense in depth without burdening the public site.
bullets: No Sentry (Vercel/Supabase dashboards)
Cross-tab realtime out of scope
Live host: horscadre-photography.vercel.app

Careers and awards are too dense for a generic marketing site.
Contact must be direct without unnecessary business backend.
Content centralized in a TypeScript data module; sectioned one-page UI.
Client i18next i18n (fr/en).
Web3Forms contact, Framer motion, Vercel Analytics.

Sports business market: roster density is the argument, not page count.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Minimal App Router (single page) and HomeScreen/UI components, more classic than 2026 feature-first projects.
next-sitemap postbuild; Vercel Analytics.
bullets: ~12 players in TypeScript
2 players with embedded video
Jest (limited coverage)

Tailwind 3 / Jest / yarn stack, assumed heritage of delivery time.
bullets: Client-side Web3Forms key = known security debt
